  • Quantum computing shows promise to help identify the most important information in complex datasets, allowing AI models to uncover useful insights with less data.
  • Potential banking applications include more accurate client modeling, improved risk assessment and detection, and more personalized client experiences.
  • Achievement positions BMO among a small group of global financial institutions exploring real-world quantum applications in the near term.

TORONTO and CHICAGO and SAN FRANCISCO, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- BMO today announced it has demonstrated quantum utility in a machine learning application using IBM quantum computers, meaning the work was performed reliably at a scale beyond what exact traditional computing methods can practically reproduce. The work explores how quantum computing could help AI models identify which information matters most in complex datasets, potentially allowing them to uncover useful insights with less data than traditional approaches.

Over time, that capability could have applications across banking, including more accurate client modeling, improved risk assessment and detection, and more personalized client experiences.

Developed in collaboration with the Democritus University of Thrace (DUTH), using IBM quantum computers, including the latest IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 processor, and reviewed by IBM's quantum research team, the achievement marks an important step in bringing quantum computing closer to practical use in financial services and ultimately creating value for clients and shareholders.

This project is part of BMO's broader strategy to responsibly apply quantum technologies to AI and machine learning applications.

"Demonstrating quantum utility is an important milestone for BMO and an exciting step forward for the broader financial services industry," said Kristin Milchanowski, Chief AI and Quantum Officer and Director, BMO Institute for Applied Artificial Intelligence & Quantum. "While we remain in the early stages of application development, these projects show how quantum computing can help solve business problems in new ways. This work builds on years of research, collaboration and innovation focused on identifying practical applications that create value for clients, employees and shareholders."

As an early investor in quantum research and one of a small number of global financial institutions applying quantum computing to real-world challenges, BMO continues to focus on practical and responsible innovations that create value for clients.

Applying Quantum Computing to Real Business Challenges

The application built by BMO and DUTH reimagines machine learning feature selection by adapting the Proxy Quantum Games framework, shifting it from a traditional classical statistical problem into a dynamic, quantum strategic game. Each feature of the dataset is a "player." A feature, or "player," scores high when it moves together with the applications' target (the model outcome variable), and low when it is uninformative or repeats other, unimportant features. The scores rank the features. This quantum game-based feature selection processes all of this on a quantum computer, and the resulting method produces results with similar quality, while only requiring one to two orders of magnitude fewer samples than traditional feature selection techniques.

"I'm excited to see BMO's progress toward real-world quantum use cases in the financial services industry, using our quantum computers to explore novel algorithmic approaches," said Scott Crowder, Vice President, IBM Quantum Adoption and Business Development.

Advancing Practical Quantum Innovation

BMO joined the IBM Quantum Network in February 2025 and continues to invest in quantum research, talent development and real-world applications. Through partnerships with the Chicago Quantum Exchange and Quantum Industry Canada, BMO is advancing practical applications of quantum computing across financial services. BMO also launched the BMO Institute for Applied Artificial Intelligence & Quantum, an enterprise-wide Centre of Excellence focused on the responsible application and governance of AI and the advancement of quantum capabilities.

"At BMO, innovation is about translating emerging technologies into meaningful business impact," said Steve Tennyson, Chief Technology and Operations Officer, BMO. "This milestone reflects years of investment in innovation, quantum computing, artificial intelligence and strategic partnerships. It demonstrates how BMO is turning emerging technologies into practical solutions that help clients improve decision-making and support long-term growth."

BMO's progress is also reflected in the 2026 Quantum Index Finance ranking, an independent benchmark of enterprise quantum readiness. BMO ranked ninth among financial institutions globally and is the highest-ranking Canadian commercial bank in the index. The ranking measures institutions in the areas of quantum workforce, research and development, and adoption.

Additionally, BMO was recently recognized by Evident AI as one of the world's top 20 banks in AI and ranked #2 among 50 banks for AI use-case outcomes - the highest-ranking Canadian bank in the category. BMO also achieved the top ranking in the Responsible AI Process indicator group, reflecting its approach to governance, risk management, employee training and operational controls.

About BMO Financial Group
BMO Financial Group is the eighth largest bank in North America by assets, with total assets of $1.5 trillion as of July 31, 2026. Serving clients for more than 200 years, BMO provides a broad range of personal and commercial banking, wealth management, global markets and investment banking products and services across Canada, the United States, and select markets globally. BMO is innovating for business value, by deploying and integrating human, digital and artificial intelligence to personalize client experiences, augment teams, and automate its business responsibly. Driven by its purpose, to Boldly Grow the Good in business and life, BMO is committed to driving positive change in the world, and making progress for a thriving economy, sustainable future, and stronger communities.

Nine Month Revenue Increased 65% and Gross Profit Increased 94%; Company on Track to Deliver First 10 MW of AI Capacity to Customer at Michigan Data Center in December 2026

LAS VEGAS, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Hyperscale Data, Inc. (NYSE American: GPUS), an artificial intelligence ("AI") data center company ("Hyperscale Data" or the "Company"), today announced financial results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 2026. Third quarter revenue increased 84% to $44.8 million, from $24.3 million in the third quarter of 2025, and gross profit increased 67% to $10.5 million, from $6.3 million from the prior year period. Revenue growth was driven by the inclusion of Gresham Worldwide, Inc. ("Gresham") following its reconsolidation in November 2025, higher lending and trading revenue, primarily from unrealized gains on equity investments, and stronger crane operations at Circle 8 Crane Services, LLC ("Circle 8").

Financial and Business Highlights

  • Revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased 84% to $44.8 million, compared to $24.3 million in the third quarter of 2025.
  • Revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased 65% to $123.8 million, compared to $75.2 million in the first nine months of 2025.
  • Gross profit for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased 94% to $34.3 million, compared to $17.7 million in the first nine months of 2025, and gross margin expanded to 27.7% from 23.5% during the same periods.
  • Circle 8 revenue increased 26% to $12.2 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026.
  • Energy segment operating income, which includes Circle 8, rose to $2.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from $450,000 in the prior year period, a nearly sixfold increase.
  • The Company remains on track to energize the first 10 megawatts ("MW") of AI capacity at its Michigan data center in December 2026, with an additional 10 MW targeted by the end of March 2027.
  • Subsequent to the quarter end, the Company received $15.0 million in gross proceeds from a convertible note financing and repaid $12.8 million of other convertible notes.

"This quarter demonstrates what our operating businesses can contribute as we build out our Michigan AI data center," said Milton "Todd" Ault III, Executive Chairman of Hyperscale Data. "Circle 8 delivered meaningful growth in both revenue and operating income. Our top priority now is commissioning our initial AI capacity and meeting our commitments to our customer, while keeping close attention on expenses and the capital required to complete our planned development."

As previously announced, the Company will host a conference call November 23, 2026, at 2:30 p.m. Pacific Time to discuss these results, followed by a broader discussion of its businesses, operating developments and strategic priorities as part of its Investor Day. All stockholders, investors and other interested parties are invited to participate and are encouraged to register using the following link: Webinar Registration - Zoom

Michigan AI Data Center Development

Through its indirect wholly owned subsidiary, Alliance Cloud Services, LLC, the Company is developing approximately 20 MW of critical AI compute capacity at its data center campus in Dowagiac, Michigan, under a master services agreement with a California-based neocloud customer. The Company ceased Bitcoin mining at the Michigan data center on September 1, 2026 for the transition to AI infrastructure services.

The agreement has an initial term of 10 years, with two five-year extension options exercisable by the customer. If the customer exercises both options and the Company meets its obligations under the agreement, the initial 20 MW deployment represents total contract value of approximately $1.2 billion over the resulting 20-year term. The customer also holds a right of first offer, exercisable within two years of the agreement's execution, on an additional 32 MW of capacity. If the customer exercises that right and both extension options, the total contract value would increase to approximately $3.0 billion.

The Company's current development targets are December 2026 for the first 10 MW and the end of March 2027 for the additional 10 MW. The schedule remains subject to financing availability, construction progress, equipment procurement, commissioning and customer deployment requirements.

While gross profit increased, higher operating expenses resulted in larger operating losses in the three- and nine-month periods ended September 30, 2026. Third quarter 2026 operating expenses were $29.9 million, compared to $20.3 million in the prior year period, primarily reflecting higher compensation, consulting and professional fees and the inclusion of Gresham. The third quarter 2026 net loss narrowed to $13.0 million from $13.6 million in the prior year period, benefiting from gains of approximately $9.2 million from changes in the fair value of crypto assets and $4.0 million from changes in the fair value of embedded derivative liabilities. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $18.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $15.3 million in the prior year period, reflecting higher preferred dividends, including $2.3 million representing the fair value of Class B common stock distributed to holders of convertible preferred stock.

The nine-month net loss also reflected significant non-cash items, principally depreciation and amortization of $18.7 million, amortization of debt discount of $6.6 million and a $4.1 million non-cash change in the participation liability, partially offset by $12.0 million of crypto asset mining revenue received in Bitcoin and a $6.2 million non-cash gain from the change in fair value of embedded derivative liabilities.

For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, operating expenses increased to $98.1 million from $48.2 million in the prior year period, reflecting the inclusion of Gresham, higher compensation, professional and consulting costs, increased marketing spending and blockchain development expenses, as well as a $2.3 million impairment of Bitcoin mining equipment and a $2.4 million loss from changes in the fair value of crypto assets. The nine month 2026 net loss of $62.1 million included a $16.1 million gain on the extinguishment of a settlement obligation and a $7.1 million impairment of restricted crypto assets.

Operating Business Performance

Circle 8. Third quarter 2026 revenue increased 26% to $12.2 million, from $9.7 million in the prior year period, supported by higher service rates and improved crane equipment utilization. Gross profit for the three months ended September 30, 2026 increased 39% to $4.7 million, and gross margin improved to 38.6% for the three months ended September 30, 2026 from 34.9% in the prior year period. Higher gross profit and lower general and administrative expenses drove the increase in Energy segment operating income. For the nine month 2026 period, crane revenue was $34.3 million compared to $35.1 million in the prior year period, reflecting lower activity from certain oil and gas customers following industry consolidation. Segment results are presented before corporate and other consolidated items.

Defense. Third quarter 2026 defense revenue was $14.6 million, compared to $1.7 million a year earlier, and nine month 2026 defense revenue was $38.4 million, compared to $5.0 million in the prior year period. The increase primarily reflected the reconsolidation of Gresham in November 2025; no Gresham revenue was included in the 2025 periods.

Lending and Trading. Third quarter 2026 revenue increased to $8.8 million from $0.1 million in the prior year period, primarily reflecting unrealized gains on investments in equity securities, partially offset by higher realized losses, with higher interest and dividend income also contributing. Cost of revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 included $4.5 million, which represents third-party participants' share of gains on investments funded through participation arrangements, resulting in segment gross profit of $4.3 million. Nine month 2026 revenue was $18.0 million, including litigation-related proceeds associated with legacy ownership interests held by Ault Lending, LLC and unrealized investment gains, and the participants' share of gains was $7.5 million. Because revenue in this segment includes realized and unrealized investment gains and losses, results can fluctuate significantly from period to period.

Hotels and Other Businesses. Revenue from Ault Global Real Estate Equities, Inc. hotel operations increased 5% to $15.2 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, driven by higher occupancy and modest improvements in average daily room rates. Other revenue for the nine months ended September 30, 2026 increased to $5.2 million from $2.2 million over the same period in the prior year, primarily from the Company's blockchain initiatives, including node software sales.

Capital and Liquidity

At September 30, 2026, total assets were $393.5 million, total liabilities were $268.3 million and total stockholders' equity, including non-controlling interest, was $125.3 million. Cash and cash equivalents were $17.3 million and restricted cash was $27.8 million. Restricted cash is available only for purposes permitted under the applicable arrangements.

Net cash used in operating activities was $8.4 million for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, compared to $24.8 million in the prior year period. Operating cash flow for the three months ended September 30, 2026 benefited from a $45.6 million increase in accounts payable and accrued expenses.

Subsequent to quarter end, the Company received aggregate gross proceeds of $15.0 million from the initial and second closings of a convertible note financing with an institutional investor on November 6 and November 18, 2026, respectively. Subject to stockholder approval and mutual agreement of the parties, the financing provides for up to an additional $10.0 million in gross proceeds. On November 6, 2026, the Company sold all of its Bitcoin holdings, approximately 211.6 Bitcoin, for gross proceeds of approximately $16.0 million. On November 16, 2026, it used approximately $14.1 million of those proceeds to repay in full convertible notes that were secured by a portion of the Bitcoin, including approximately $12.8 million of principal and a $1.3 million prepayment premium.

The Company continues to require substantial additional financing to complete the Michigan deployment, fund operations and meet existing obligations. At September 30, 2026, current liabilities exceeded current assets by approximately $128.1 million, and the Company's financial statements disclosed substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern that has not been alleviated. Management is pursuing financing, asset monetizations and other strategic transactions to address these requirements.

Investors should review the Company's Quarterly Report on Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2026, filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on November 18, 2026, for the complete financial statements, notes, liquidity discussion and risk factors.

For more information on Hyperscale Data and its subsidiaries, Hyperscale Data recommends that stockholders, investors and any other interested parties read Hyperscale Data's public filings and press releases available under the Investor Relations section at hyperscaledata.com or available at www.sec.gov.

About Hyperscale Data, Inc.

Through its wholly owned subsidiary Sentinum, Inc., Hyperscale Data owns and operates a data center at which it offers colocation and hosting services for the emerging AI ecosystems and other industries. Another of Hyperscale Data's wholly owned subsidiaries, Ault Capital Group, Inc. ("ACG"), is a hybrid private equity firm and operating company that acquires, finances, builds and actively manages businesses across financial services, digital assets, industrial services, hospitality, defense technologies and other sectors.

Hyperscale Data currently expects the divestiture of ACG (the "Divestiture") to occur in 2027. Upon the occurrence of the Divestiture, the Company would be an owner and operator of data centers to support high-performance computing services, as well as a holder of the digital assets and the third wholly owned subsidiary of the Company, Omnipresent Robotics, LLC. Until the Divestiture occurs, the Company will continue to provide, through ACG and its wholly and majority-owned subsidiaries and strategic investments, mission-critical products that support a diverse range of industries, including an AI software platform, equipment rental services, defense/aerospace, industrial, automotive and hotel operations. In addition, ACG is actively engaged in private credit and structured finance through Ault Lending, LLC, a licensed lending subsidiary. Hyperscale Data's headquarters are located at 11411 Southern Highlands Parkway, Suite 190, Las Vegas, NV 89141.

On December 23, 2024, the Company issued one million (1,000,000) shares of a newly designated Series F Exchangeable Preferred Stock (the "Series F Preferred Stock") to all common stockholders and holders of the Series C Preferred Stock on an as-converted basis. The Divestiture will occur through the voluntary exchange of the Series F Preferred Stock for shares of Class A Common Stock and Class B Common Stock of ACG (collectively, the "ACG Shares"). The Company reminds its stockholders that only those holders of the Series F Preferred Stock who agree to surrender such shares, and do not properly withdraw such surrender, in the exchange offer through which the Divestiture will occur, will be entitled to receive the ACG Shares and consequently be shareholders of ACG upon the occurrence of the Divestiture.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Torex Resources Inc. (the "Company" or "Torex") (TSX: TXR) (NYSE: TXR) announces that it has received approval from the Toronto Stock Exchange (the "TSX") of its notice of intention to renew its normal course issuer bid (the "NCIB").

Under the NCIB, Torex is authorized to purchase up to 7,176,403 of its common shares ("Common Shares"), representing approximately 10% of the public float as of November 11, 2026, during the period commencing on November 23, 2026 and ending on November 22, 2027. As of November 11, 2026, Torex had a total of 90,251,272 Common Shares issued and outstanding and a public float of 71,764,036 Common Shares.

The NCIB provides Torex with the flexibility to acquire Common Shares from time to time as an effective means of returning capital to its shareholders in accordance with its corporate strategy. Outside of blackout periods, Common Shares may be purchased under the NCIB based on the discretion of the Company's management, in compliance with the rules of the TSX and applicable securities laws.

Purchases under the NCIB will be made on the open market through the facilities of the TSX, the New York Stock Exchange (the "NYSE") or alternative trading systems in Canada or the United States at prevailing market prices. The number of Common Shares that can be purchased pursuant to the NCIB on the TSX is subject to a current daily maximum of 129,854 Common Shares (which is equal to 25% of the average daily trading volume of 519,418 Common Shares on the TSX for the six full calendar months ending October 31, 2026), subject to the Company's ability to make one block purchase of Common Shares per calendar week that exceeds such limits. Purchases on the NYSE or alternative trading systems in the United States will be subject to daily limitations and other conditions regarding the manner, timing, price and volume of purchases in order to qualify for the safe harbor provided under applicable United States securities laws. All Common Shares purchased under the NCIB will be cancelled after their purchase. The Company intends to fund any purchases under the NCIB from its available working capital.

Additionally, the Company has entered into an automatic share purchase plan ("ASPP") with its designated broker to facilitate the purchase of Common Shares under the NCIB at times when the Company would ordinarily not be permitted to purchase its shares due to regulatory restrictions and ordinary course of business self-imposed blackout periods. Pursuant to the ASPP, prior to entering into a blackout period, the Company may, but is not required to, instruct the designated broker to make purchases under the NCIB in accordance with the terms of the ASPP. Such purchases will be determined by the designated broker in its sole discretion based on parameters established by the Company prior to the blackout period in accordance with the rules of the TSX, applicable securities laws and the terms of the ASPP.

Under Torex's current NCIB, which commenced on November 21, 2025 and ends on November 20, 2026, the Company obtained approval to purchase up to a total of 8,133,430 Common Shares, of which 6,260,801 Common Shares were purchased through the facilities of the TSX at a volume weighted average price of approximately C$68.08 (excluding commissions) per Common Share as of November 11, 2026.

Although Torex has the present intention to acquire its Common Shares pursuant to the NCIB, the Company will not be obligated to make any purchases and purchases may be suspended by the Company at any time. Decisions regarding any future repurchases will depend on certain factors, such as market conditions, share price, and other opportunities to invest capital for growth.

About Torex

Torex is a Canadian mining company engaged in the production, development, and exploration of gold, copper, and silver from its flagship Morelos Complex in Guerrero, Mexico. The Company also owns the Los Reyes gold-silver project in Sinaloa, Mexico and a portfolio of early-stage exploration projects, including Batopilas and Guigui in Chihuahua, Mexico, La Gloria in Sonora, Mexico, and Medicine Springs in Nevada, USA, as well as an option to acquire the Gryphon Summit project in Nevada, USA.

The Company's key strategic objectives are: optimize Morelos production and costs; disciplined growth and capital allocation; grow reserves and resources; project delivery excellence; retain and attract best industry talent; and be an industry leader in responsible mining. In addition to realizing the full potential of the Morelos property, the Company continues to seek opportunities to acquire assets that enable diversification and deliver value to shareholders.

Toronto, Ontario--(Newsfile Corp. - November 19, 2026) - Happy Belly Food Group Inc. (CSE: HBFG) (OTCQB: HBFGF) ("Happy Belly" or the "Company"), a leader in acquiring and scaling emerging food brands is pleased to announce its unaudited financial results and corporate update for the fiscal quarter ended September 30th, 2026.

Q3 2026 financial and recent business highlights

System-wide sales growth:

  • Happy Belly generated system-wide sales across its Quick Service Restaurant ("QSR") portfolio of $31.0 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, representing an increase of approximately 61% compared to $19.2 million in the same quarter of fiscal 2025.

  • The continued increase in system-wide sales reflects a combination of organic sales growth across the Company's existing restaurant base and the continued expansion of its restaurant network.

  • As at September 30, 2026, the Company had 110 operating restaurants, representing an increase of approximately 51% from 73 operating restaurants in the same quarter of fiscal 2025.

Revenue growth:

  • Total operating revenues, services and rebates were $8.2 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, representing an increase of approximately 19% compared to $6.9 million in the same quarter of fiscal 2025.

    The year-over-year increase reflects continued growth in the Company's QSR operations, increased revenues generated from a larger restaurant network, and incremental royalties and franchise-related revenues resulting from new restaurant openings.

Product sales and franchise revenue:

  • Total product sales were $5.9 million in the third quarter of fiscal 2026, representing an increase of approximately 2% compared to $5.8 million in the same quarter of fiscal 2025.

  • Royalties and franchise fee revenues increased to $1.6 million during the third quarter of fiscal 2026, representing growth of approximately 49% compared to $1.1 million in the same quarter of fiscal 2025. 

    The significant increase in royalties and franchise fees reflects the continued expansion of Happy Belly's franchised restaurant base and the corresponding increase in system-wide sales upon which royalty revenues are generated.

Adjusted EBITDA:

  • Adjusted EBITDA(1) was $1.02 million, representing an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 12.5%, during the third quarter of fiscal 2026, compared to $0.7 million and an Adjusted EBITDA margin of 10.1% in the same quarter of fiscal 2025.

  • Adjusted EBITDA increased on an absolute dollar basis alongside the significant growth in revenue and system-wide sales, Adjusted EBITDA margin increased by approximately 2.4 percentage points year over year, from 10.1% to 12.5%. The improvement in margin reflects the higher contribution from royalties and franchise fee revenues, which increased approximately 49% year over year, while direct operating costs were relatively flat at $2.9 million in both periods.

    Management continues to focus on generating operating leverage as the Company's restaurant base and recurring royalty revenue continues to scale.

Strong cash position:

  • The Company maintained a strong liquidity position, with cash and cash equivalents of approximately $11.6 million as at September 30, 2026, compared to approximately $3.0 million as at December 31, 2025. The strengthened cash position provides Happy Belly with financial flexibility to continue supporting its organic growth initiatives while maintaining sufficient liquidity to support the Company's ongoing operations and working capital requirements.

Management Commentary
"In Q3 we delivered record QSR system-wide sales, achieved a record restaurant store count, focused on operational efficiency, franchisee profitability, U.S. expansion, and ended the quarter with a strong cash balance, all done while making smart allocations of capital investments back into our business. We are continuing our momentum into the last quarter of 2026 with more store openings on the way as we continue to accelerate growth. We are just getting started," said Sean Black, Chief Executive Officer of Happy Belly Food Group.

Business Update
During the third quarter of 2026, Happy Belly announced 13 restaurant openings and added an additional 5 restaurants through M&A across its portfolio, including nine Heal Wellness locations and four Rosie's Burgers locations. Heal Wellness opened its first Vancouver Island restaurant in British Columbia.

On October 3rd, Happy Belly announced the grand opening of Heal Wellness's first U.S. restaurant in Lubbock, Texas. Building on that opening, Happy Belly announced on November 2, that The Curative Group had increased their commitment from a 10-unit Texas development commitment to 150 locations statewide.

The Company also announced 12 newly secured restaurant sites, comprising nine for Heal Wellness, two for Yolks Breakfast and one for Rosie's Burgers. Franchise development also advanced with the first New Brunswick franchise agreements for Heal Wellness in Moncton and Rosie's Burgers in Fredericton, along with a new Via Cibo franchise agreement in Kingston, Ontario.

Happy Belly completed one acquisition during the quarter, acquiring a 50% interest in Ghost Taco through a joint venture with the right to acquire the remaining 50%. PRESIDENT'S MESSAGE

In Q3 2026, Coelacanth produced an average of 4,773 boe/d which was materially affected by turnarounds of the Westcoast pipeline and the McMahon gas plant that resulted in all of Coelacanth's production being shut-in from September 7th to October 21st. Production was fully restored as of the end of October and is currently estimated at 6,459 boe/d (25% oil and NGLs). Production from the new four-well 9-32 pad will be additive to this once on-stream.

Capital operations for Q3 and Q4 2026 focused on the drilling and completion of the 9-32 pad at Two Rivers East and completion of the 12-27 Lower Montney well at Two Rivers West. Coelacanth has just started flowing back the frac water from the 9-32 pad with expected test results to be released within the next few weeks.

The 9-32 pad includes three Lower Montney development wells plus an Upper Montney well that is a major step-out (seven miles toe to toe) from the successful B5-19 Upper Montney well previously drilled. A successful step-out at 9-32 would prove out a very material geographic area for reserve bookings as no undeveloped locations were booked to the greater area as at the end of 2025. The three Lower Montney wells, if successful, would also prove up additional acreage while providing valuable data to optimize future wells from both a cost and recovery perspective. The 12-27 well test has not yet been completed.

The long-term view for LNG expansion in British Columbia is very positive for Coelacanth's land. Coelacanth delivers its gas to the Westcoast pipeline that has a direct connection to Coastal GasLink and LNG Canada which recently announced FID of Phase II that will double its current capacity. Other planned and likely projects will only add to the demand for natural gas particularly in British Columbia. Both the federal and provincial governments have also stated support for further LNG developments that should help attract capital to these projects.

Coelacanth believes that lands that have scale and direct access to Coastal GasLink such as Coelacanth's 150 section contiguous block of Montney (estimated to hold 6.9 billion barrels of Discovered Oil Initially-In-Place (IIP) and 5.9 trillion cubic feet of Discovered Gas IIP plus 8.3 billion barrels of Undiscovered Oil IIP and 7.1 trillion cubic feet of Undiscovered Gas IIP) (1) will become increasingly valuable once proven up and ownership of potential LNG expansions are solidified.

Total Petroleum Initially-In-Place is that quantity of petroleum that is estimated to exist originally in naturally occurring accumulations. It includes that quantity of petroleum that is estimated, as of a given date, to be contained in known accumulations, prior to production, plus those estimated quantities in accumulations yet to be discovered (equivalent to "total resources").

Discovered Petroleum Initially-In-Place (equivalent to discovered resources) is that quantity of petroleum that is estimated, as of a given date, to be contained in known accumulations prior to production. The recoverable portion of discovered petroleum initially in place includes production, reserves, and contingent resources; the remainder is unrecoverable.

Reserves are estimated remaining quantities of oil and natural gas and related substances anticipated to be recoverable from known accumulations, as of a given date, based on the analysis of drilling, geological, geophysical, and engineering data; the use of established technology; and specified economic conditions, which are generally accepted as being reasonable. Reserves are further classified according to the level of certainty associated with the estimates and may be subclassified based on development and production status.

Contingent Resources are those quantities of petroleum estimated, as of a given date, to be potentially recoverable from known accumulations using established technology or technology under development, but which are not currently considered to be commercially recoverable due to one or more contingencies. Contingencies may include factors such as economic, legal, environmental, political, and regulatory matters, or a lack of markets. It is also appropriate to classify as contingent resources the estimated discovered recoverable quantities associated with a project in the early evaluation stage. Contingent Resources are further classified in accordance with the level of certainty associated with the estimates and may be subclassified based on project maturity and/or characterized by their economic status.

Undiscovered Petroleum Initially-In-Place (equivalent to undiscovered resources) is that quantity of petroleum that is estimated, on a given date, to be contained in accumulations yet to be discovered. The recoverable portion of undiscovered petroleum initially in place is referred to as "prospective resources," the remainder as "unrecoverable."

Prospective Resources are those quantities of petroleum estimated, as of a given date, to be potentially recoverable from undiscovered accumulations by application of future development projects. Prospective resources have both an associated chance of discovery and a chance of development. Prospective Resources are further subdivided in accordance with the level of certainty associated with recoverable estimates assuming their discovery and development and may be subclassified based on project maturity.

There is no certainty that any portion of the resources will be discovered. If discovered, there is no certainty that it will be commercially viable to produce any portion of the resources. The key variables relevant to the evaluation are porosity, reservoir thickness, pressure, water saturation and gas composition which have increasing uncertainty, both positive and negative, with distance from existing wells.

VANCOUVER, British Columbia, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Newcore Gold Ltd. ("Newcore" or the "Company") (TSX-V: NCAU, OTCQX: NCAUF) is pleased to announce the submission of a Mining Lease application for the Company's Enchi Gold Project ("Enchi" or the "Project") in Ghana. The Mining Lease application covers 53.37 km2 of the 248 km2 property.

Honourable Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, Minister for Lands & Natural Resources, Ghana stated, "The Government of Ghana welcomes Newcore's submission of a Mining Lease application for the Enchi Gold Project. The Project is one of the most advanced large-scale gold projects in development in Ghana and has the potential to create long-term benefits through job creation, local community support and contribution to national revenues. VANCOUVER, British-Columbia, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- VR Resources Limited (“VR” or the “Company”, TSX.V: VRR, FSE: 5VR; OTCQB: VRRCF) is pleased to announce that the follow-up drill program planned for its New Boston copper-moly-tungsten-silver porphyry-skarn project in Nevada is now underway. 


Photo 1. Earth work on site at New Boston last week, in preparation for the drilling that is now underway, in follow-up to the 2,892 ft intersection of polyphase stockwork veining in NB26-003 completed in June and located some 450 metres to the right of this photo. Planned drill holes all benefit from the array of pre-existing roads and trails on the property that are evident in this photo. 

Four to six holes are planned in follow-up to drill hole NB26-003 completed in June which intersected 317 m at 0.77% CuEq*, starting at surface, above 419 m of 0.48% CuEq*, in 2,892 ft (881 m) of continuous polymetallic stockwork veining with moly, copper, tungsten and silver mineralization (NR on Aug. 26, 2026). 

Each planned hole is expected to take 3 – 4 weeks to complete, with results expected through Q1, 2027. 

Each planned hole is collared in mineralized stockwork veins exposed on surface (see Photo 1), similar to NB26-003, which did not hit the bottom of the mineral system through 2,892 ft of drilling.

Overall, the Company has the flexibility to drill on an array of 16 potential sites shown in Figure 1, as identified on its NOI permit with the BLM (Bureau of Land Management). The permitted drill sites span the Jeep Mine area of high DCIP chargeability in the western half of the overall polymetallic porphyry-skarn vein and dyke system exposed on surface over a 3-4 km strike at New Boston.


Figure 1. Blue circles are locations of the 16 drill sites approved in the NOI drill permit for Jeep Mine. Shown is the drill collar and trace for drill hole NB26-003 completed in June. Base map is from the 3D-array DCIP geophysical survey completed at New Boston in 2023, showing IP iso-shells on a conductivity base map, 200m depth slice. Chargeability values at the Jeep Mine range from 15–21 mV/V. Mineralized sheeted veins strike for 2,100 m east-west across Jeep Mine through East Zone.


Figure 2. View east at Jeep Mine from the Blue Ribbon skarns located to the west, at the western end of the 3-4 km skarn and porphyry system at New Boston. Note the array of historic roads and trails available for the follow-up drilling that is now underway. The permitted drill sites shown on the corresponding map in Figure 1 span a strike length of approximately 800 m eastward from NB26-003 at Jeep Mine. Follow-up drilling will test for the eastward continuation of the upper, tungsten bearing mineral interval in NB26-003, in the deep red-brown garnet alteration visible in this photo in front of the drill, and running up the ridgeline and hill to the east. The alteration occurs in host-rock Triassic limestone recrystallized to marble, invaded by multiple phases of porphyry dykes, and crosscut by polyphase stockwork veining.

From Dr. Michael Gunning, Chief Executive Officer of the Company: “We are excited to have a crew and rig back on site at New Boston; the drill is turning! We are executing immediately on the stated use of proceeds from our recent financings in pursuit of near-term value creation potential at the drill bit for our shareholders.

Our goal with this program is to evaluate the lateral extent and volume potential of the mineralization encountered in NB26-003, in all three dimensions. More specifically, the planned follow-up holes are designed to test:

1. the continuation of the tungsten-bearing upper mineral interval in NB26-003 for a strike length of 400 - 500 m to the east (see Figure 2);

2. the depth potential of the mineral system beyond the veining and mineralization extending from surface through the 2,892 ft completed in hole NB26-003, open;

3. the down-dip extent of mineralization in sheeted veins to the north of NB26-003, in relation to the north-dipping host-rock Triassic limestone that is invaded by the Cretaceous-aged polyphase porphyry system.

We are ready. Modeling for this drill program is the result of three years of detailed surface exploration and state-of-the-art airborne and ground geophysical surveys by VR, built upon expert all-be-it sporadic historical work in the 1960’s and 70’s, and culminating in the 2,892 ft intersection in NB26-003 in June.”

Short field videos recorded during the recent CEO site-visit to New Boston are available on the New Boston Project Page on the Company’s website at www.vrr.ca. They further illustrate the key messages for New Boston around vein intensity, road access on the property, the strength of local infrastructure, and the long-standing history and pedigree of the exploration and mining industry in Nevada. Descriptions of the location, geology and history of New Boston can also be found on the Project Page, along with maps, sections, and outcrop, hand sample and drill core photographs.

This third-party RCL validation program strengthens Temas' technology licensing strategy, while a seasoned ASX director and audit partner joins the Board to support commercialization of the RCL Platform

Highlights

  • Temas Resources Corp. ("Temas" or the "Company") has entered into a contract to provide Regenerative Chloride Leach ("RCL") Platform Technology validation services to an arm's-length mineral company (the "Counterparty"), following the successful Stage 1 validation program completed with SAGA Metals Corp. ("SAGA").
  • The Counterparty's project is located in Québec, in close proximity to Temas' wholly owned La Blache Titanium-Vanadium Project and to the proposed RCL demonstration plant site in Baie-Comeau, Québec.
  • The program will follow the same stage-gate framework used for SAGA, beginning with a Stage 1 bench-scale validation of the RCL Platform on representative samples supplied by the Counterparty.
  • The Stage 1 program carries an estimated contract value of approximately CAD$50,000 and is expected to be completed approximately seven weeks after receipt of samples and notice to proceed.
  • The Counterparty has requested to remain anonymous until Stage 1 validation work is complete. Temas will identify the Counterparty and report the results once Stage 1 is concluded.
  • The Company also announces the appointment of Mr. Anthony Travers as a Director. As a Chartered Accountant and ASX Board Director, Anthony brings approximately 40 years of senior leadership, including an extensive career with KPMG Australia and as a partner at Sydney-based audit firm Hall Chadwick, as well as significant experience working with companies in the mining sector.
  • Mr. Kobi Ben Shabat and Mr. Nic Matich have resigned as Directors for personal reasons and reduced time availability. One Board position remains open for a future appointment.

Why this Matters to Investors

1) Another Third-Party Validation Opportunity for the RCL Platform

The contract extends the commercial validation of the RCL Platform to another independent mineral company, supporting Temas' strategy of building a technology licensing and services business alongside its wholly owned mineral assets.

2) Regional Proximity Creates Strategic Optionality

The Counterparty's project lies near both La Blache and the proposed Baie-Comeau demonstration plant site. Should validation be successful, this proximity may support shared infrastructure, regional feed opportunities and a more efficient pathway to demonstration-scale processing in Québec.

3) Board Renewal Aligned with Commercialization

Mr. Travers brings strong corporate governance and audit experience at a time when the Company's primary focus is commercializing the RCL technology and accelerating its planned growth.

VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / Temas Resources Corp. (ASX:TIO)(CSE:TMAS)(OTCQB:TMASF)(FSE:26P0) is pleased to announce that the Company has entered into a contract on November 16, 2026, with an arm's-length mineral exploration and development company to provide RCL validation services, similar to those recently completed for SAGA Metals Corp. The counterparty to this agreement is a Québec-based private company with a mineral exploration project focussed primarily on titanium, iron and phosphorus and located near the Company's La Blache property and proposed RCL demonstration plant in Baie-Comeau, Québec. At the same time, the Company also announces changes to its Board of Directors.

RCL Validation Services Contract

Under the contract, Temas will evaluate the application of its proprietary RCL Platform on representative mineralization supplied by the counterparty, using a structured stage-gate framework consistent with the SAGA program. Stage 1 is expected to comprise preliminary bench-scale testwork under standardized RCL operating conditions to assess extraction behaviour of the target metals and the suitability of the RCL Platform for future commercial development on the Counterparty's mineralization.

The Counterparty's VTM/Ilmenite project is located in Québec and is in close proximity to Temas' La Blache Project and to the proposed RCL demonstration plant site in Baie-Comeau. The Counterparty has asked that its identity remain confidential at this stage. Temas has agreed to this request and expects to disclose the Counterparty's name, together with Stage 1 results, once the Stage 1 validation work is complete.

Success at Stage 1 would be followed by a Gate 1 process applicability review. A positive Gate 1 decision would allow the project to advance to a Detailed Bench Optimization Program (Stage 2), followed by potential mini-pilot (Stage 3) and demonstration plant (Stage 4) programs, each subject to its own gate review. There is no assurance that Stage 1 will meet its objectives or that any subsequent stage will proceed.

Key Terms of the Stage 1 Program

ProgramStage 1 bench-scale scoping program applying the RCL process to three concentrate samples supplied by the Counterparty
TestworkSix leach tests (one double-stage RCL leach validation test on each sample) at Temas' historical base-case conditions, supported by head chemistry, particle size and mineralogical characterization (QEMSCAN and XRD)
Target metalsPrincipally titanium and iron
Contract valueEstimated C$52,876, including a 15% contingency on a C$45,979 base
Payment terms50% on contract execution, 40% on completion of Stage 1 testwork and 10% within 30 days of submission of the Stage 1 report
TimingApproximately seven weeks from receipt of samples and notice to proceed
DeliverablesTechnical report covering metal extractions, residue characterization, reagent consumption and recommendations, together with a results presentation to the Counterparty's technical team and a Gate 1 review
OwnershipTest data and reports become the property of the Counterparty on payment in full for Stage 1. Temas retains all rights in the RCL process and in any improvements arising from the testwork that relate to it.

Stage 1 does not include optimization of leach parameters. Its purpose is to confirm whether the RCL process is applicable to the Counterparty's materials under Temas' historical base-case conditions and to guide any subsequent optimization work.

Tim Fernback, President & Chief Executive Officer, commented:

"Following the successful validation of RCL on SAGA's mineralization, we are pleased to sign another third-party validation contract, this time with a company whose project is close to La Blache and to our proposed Baie-Comeau demonstration plant site. That proximity is strategically important. If Stage 1 is successful, it opens the door to a regional processing opportunity in Québec and further demonstrates the RCL Platform as a technology that can be licensed and deployed across multiple projects. We look forward to naming our client and reporting results once Stage 1 is complete."

Board Changes

Mr. Kobi Ben Shabat and Mr. Nic Matich have resigned as Directors of Temas, effective November 15, 2026, for personal reasons and reduced time commitments. The Board thanks both Mr. Ben Shabat and Mr. Matich for their service and contribution to the Company and wishes them well in their future endeavours.

The Board is pleased to welcome Mr. Anthony Travers, CA as a Director, effective immediately. Following these changes, one Board position remains open and the Company expects to fill it with a future appointment. For this remaining board position, the Company is looking for an experienced senior executive that can assist in the commercialization of the high-growth RCL business plan.

About Anthony Travers

Mr. Travers is a highly experienced Chartered Accountant with more than 40 years of leadership across professional services, corporate governance and the mining sector. He spent approximately 30 years with KPMG Australia, rising to Lead Partner & National Industry Leader for the Hospitality & Leisure Division. He is currently and investor and partner of Hall Chadwick, a successful Sydney-based Australian audit and consulting firm, and has served as a director of ASX-listed companies. He brings a strong corporate governance and audit background to the Temas Board.

Mr. Travers currently serves as Non-Executive Director (Finance, Governance and Risk) of SecureLink Networks Ltd, a cybersecurity and connectivity solutions provider, and as Chairperson of Redivium Ltd, which is licensing recognised battery recycling technology across Europe. He is also a Resident Director for multinational groups operating in Australia, including Accelya Group and Riversdale Mining, and through Active Directions and WTS Australia provides CFO advisory services to businesses on growth, operational efficiency, investor readiness and complex financial matters. He has chaired Asset Recruitment, a finance and accounting recruitment business, since 2018, and is a founding investor in G&G Advisory Partners, a mergers and acquisitions advisory firm. He was previously Chairman of iMoney Holdings, an Australian public unlisted corporate advisory and funds management business.

Tim Fernback, President & Chief Executive Officer, commented:

"On behalf of the Board and management, I thank Kobi and Nic for their service and support of Temas. As the Company matures and grows, it is important that the Board continues to evolve and brings the skills and experience to support our next phase, with commercializing the RCL technology, our primary focus. Anthony's audit, governance and ASX experience, and his long track record with junior mining companies, make him an excellent fit, and we are delighted to welcome him."

Anthony Travers, Non-Executive Director, commented:

"I'm excited to join the Temas Board during this period of growth centred around the commercialization and scale up of its patented RCL metallurgical technology platform. With 10 years of local company Directorship and over 40 years of international audit experience, I feel that I can add both a strong network of contacts for future business development and valuable guidance as the company enters this hyper-growth phase."

Building a Commercial Technology Platform

Temas combines ownership of its La Blache and Lac Brûlé titanium-vanadium-iron projects in Québec with the commercialization of its proprietary RCL Platform. The Company believes that successful validation across multiple third-party projects has the potential to generate future revenues through technology licensing, engineering services, strategic partnerships and commercial processing agreements. The new contract and the strengthened Board are both aimed at advancing that objective.

About Temas Resources Corp.

Temas Resources Corp. (ASX:TIO)(CSE:TMAS)(OTCQB:TMASF)(FSE:26P0) is advancing the commercialization of its proprietary Regenerative Chloride Leach ("RCL") Platform Technology while developing a portfolio of critical mineral assets in North America.

The Company's RCL Platform is designed to recover titanium, vanadium, iron and other critical minerals using a regenerative mixed chloride leaching process intended to improve recoveries, reduce reagent consumption and provide an environmentally responsible alternative to conventional extraction technologies.

In addition to advancing its wholly owned La Blache Titanium-Vanadium Project in Québec and other strategic mineral assets, Temas is pursuing commercialization opportunities for the RCL Platform through technology licensing, strategic partnerships and collaborative development programs with mining companies seeking innovative processing solutions for complex critical mineral deposits.

Twilio Segment gives Chelsea a more connected view of its global fanbase for real-time responses to personal interests and match moments on the pitch

LONDON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Twilio (NYSE: TWLO), the infrastructure for customer engagement in the AI era, kicked off its SIGNAL World Tour London, by unveiling that Chelsea Football Club has slashed campaign launch times from 48 hours to under 15 minutes with Twilio Segment.

Building a Single View of the Global Fan

Chelsea’s global fans interact with the Club across matchdays, ticketing, its mobile app, ecommerce and other digital experiences. Historically, these interactions sat across siloed systems, creating duplicate customer records for a single fan. By consolidating its data, Chelsea removed over 460,000 duplicate records. With this cleaner and unified fan database, campaign launch time has been reduced from 48+ hours to under 15 minutes.

Beyond the Pitch: Elevating the Fan Experience

Chelsea is now able to send its fans highly relevant messages tailored to them right as the action happens on the pitch. With Twilio Segment, Chelsea is able to:

  • Create Real-Time Offers: After Estêvão Willian’s extraordinary goal during the 3-0 victory vs Barcelona in November 2025, Chelsea used Twilio Segment to identify fans who had selected Estêvão as their favourite player during mobile app onboarding. Chelsea triggered a real-time, personalised "Blue Friday" email offer, driving a 60% increase in conversion rates compared to standard seasonal benchmarks.
  • Predict Fan Purchases: To support the restock of the sold-out 2025/26 Third Kit, Chelsea leveraged Twilio Segment’s Predictive Audiences, which analysed historical purchasing behaviour and made predictions of which fans were most likely to buy. This data informed a Meta-sponsored ads campaign, generating a 16% click-rate uplift over standard campaigns and delivering a five-figure incremental revenue gain.
  • Use data-driven approaches for paid marketing: During the 2025/26 season, Chelsea continued to use Segment’s Predictive models to inform its paid media strategy. Chelsea saw an increased paid media return on ad spend of 22% and paid media revenue rose 75%, year-on-year.

Phil Lynch, Chief Digital Officer for Chelsea Football Club, said: “Our supporters don’t experience Chelsea through a single channel. They might be at Stamford Bridge, following a match from another country, using our app or interacting with Chelsea online. Our ambition is to connect those experiences so we can better understand what matters to individual supporters and make every interaction with Chelsea more relevant to the fan. Working with Twilio is helping us turn those different touchpoints into a more connected relationship with our fans across the world.”

Peter Bell, Vice President of EMEA Marketing at Twilio, said: “Marketing needs to be personal. When you have the right context, you can drive fan interaction. By shifting from legacy data silos to Twilio's context rich architecture, Chelsea has eliminated the lag between a real-world match event and commercial activation. Being able to capture fan demand at the moment of 'peak emotion', and launching campaigns in under 15 minutes instead of 48+ hours, is exactly how modern brands should drive sustainable ROI. With Twilio, Chelsea is demonstrating what engagement looks like at scale, with measurable results for the organisation.”

Chelsea plans to build on the programme during the 2026/27 season by developing targeted propensity and customer lifetime value predictive models, as well as by integrating systems more broadly within the Club. Following the success of early integrations, Chelsea is advancing towards additional real-time matchday interactions, with examples including special offers being triggered the moment a fan scans their ticket at the physical turnstile. By merging real-world movements with digital marketing, Chelsea and Twilio will continue to make the fan experience seamless and highly relevant.

Despite weaker operating performance, the Bloomsbury-Covent Garden-Soho submarket topped London’s hotel investment rankings in October, according to data from CoStar, a global leading provider of online real estate marketplaces, information and analytics in the property markets.

Large single asset deals drive over £1 billion in sales

Trailing sales volume reached approximately £771 million by September. The £300 million sale of the Rosewood London lifted the total above £1 billion in October. International capital accounted for 85% of local acquisitions over the past 12 months.

HANGZHOU, China, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Youdao, Inc. ("Youdao" or the "Company") (NYSE: DAO), an AI solutions provider specializing in learning and advertising, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Highlights

  • Total net revenues were RMB1.4 billion (US$213.1 million), representing a 12.3% decrease from the same period in 2025.
    - Net revenues from learning services were RMB609.4 million (US$90.9 million), representing a 5.2% decrease from the same period in 2025.
    - Net revenues from smart devices were RMB145.2 million (US$21.7 million), representing a 40.9% decrease from the same period in 2025.
    - Net revenues from online marketing services were RMB674.3 million (US$100.6 million), representing an 8.8% decrease from the same period in 2025.
  • Gross margin was 43.6%, compared with 42.2% for the same period in 2025.
  • Income from operations was RMB33.7 million (US$5.0 million), representing a 19.2% increase from the same period in 2025.
  • Basic and diluted net income per American depositary share ("ADS") attributable to ordinary shareholders were RMB0.28 (US$0.04), compared with near zero for the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS attributable to ordinary shareholders were RMB0.38 (US$0.06), compared with RMB0.08 for the same period of 2025.

"In the third quarter, we achieved operating profitability for the ninth consecutive quarter, reflecting the continued strength of our business. The strong reception of our newly launched Confucius speech and translation models in the global open-source community further demonstrated our leadership in real-time speech AI," said Dr. Feng Zhou, Chief Executive Officer and Director of Youdao.

"Looking ahead, we will continue advancing our AI-Native Strategy, leveraging Confucius LLM to develop compelling products, deepen user engagement, and drive sustainable growth. We remain confident in meeting our full-year financial objectives, with continued improvements in operating profit and cash flow," Dr. Zhou concluded.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Net Revenues 

Net revenues for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB1.4 billion (US$213.1 million), representing a 12.3% decrease from RMB1.6 billion for the same period of 2025.

Net revenues from learning services were RMB609.4 million (US$90.9 million) for the third quarter of 2026, representing a 5.2% decrease from RMB643.1 million for the same period of 2025.

Net revenues from smart devices were RMB145.2 million (US$21.7 million) for the third quarter of 2026, representing a 40.9% decrease from RMB245.8 million for the same period of 2025, primarily due to a decline in demand for smart learning devices.

Net revenues from online marketing services were RMB674.3 million (US$100.6 million) for the third quarter of 2026, representing an 8.8% decrease from RMB739.7 million for the same period of 2025. The year-over-year decrease reflects Youdao's disciplined, strategic approach to engagement acceptance, which places greater emphasis on higher ROI (return on investment) engagements. Youdao believes this strategy has enhanced the overall operational efficiency of its business.

Gross Profit and Gross Margin

Gross profit for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB622.7 million (US$92.9 million), representing a 9.5% decrease from RMB687.9 million for the same period of 2025. Gross margin was 43.6% for the third quarter of 2026, compared with 42.2% for the same period of 2025.

Gross margin for learning services was 59.7% for the third quarter of 2026, compared with 58.5% for the same period of 2025.

Gross margin for smart devices was 41.0% for the third quarter of 2026, compared with 50.3% for the same period of 2025. The decrease was mainly attributable to increased bill-of-materials cost for smart devices.

Gross margin for online marketing services was 29.6% for the third quarter of 2026, compared with 25.4% for the same period of 2025. The improvement was mainly attributable to improved gross margin profile of performance-based advertisements through third parties' internet properties compared with the same period of last year.

Operating Expenses

Total operating expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB589.0 million (US$87.9 million), compared with RMB659.6 million for the same period of last year.

Sales and marketing expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB422.2 million (US$63.0 million), representing a decrease of 13.4% from RMB487.7 million for the same period of 2025. This decrease was attributable to the reduced marketing expenditures in smart devices.

Research and development expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB118.3 million (US$17.6 million), representing a decrease of 7.4% from RMB127.8 million for the same period of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to the decreased headcount for research and development employees, leading to payroll savings.

General and administrative expenses for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB48.5 million (US$7.2 million), representing an increase of 10.0% from RMB44.1 million for the same period of 2025. The increase was mainly attributable to an increase in expected credit losses on the Company's accounts receivables.

Income from Operations

As a result of the foregoing, income from operations for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB33.7 million (US$5.0 million), increasing by 19.2% from RMB28.3 million for the same period in 2025. The margin of income from operations was 2.4%, compared with 1.7% for the same period of last year.

Net Income Attributable to Youdao's Ordinary Shareholders

Net income attributable to Youdao's ordinary shareholders for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB33.4 million (US$5.0 million), compared with RMB0.1 million for the same period of last year. Non-GAAP net income attributable to Youdao's ordinary shareholders for the third quarter of 2026 was RMB45.9 million (US$6.8 million), increasing by nearly 4 times from RMB9.2 million for the same period of last year.

Basic and diluted net income per ADS attributable to ordinary shareholders for the third quarter of 2026 were RMB0.28 (US$0.04), compared with near zero for the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP basic and diluted net income per ADS attributable to ordinary shareholders were RMB0.38 (US$0.06), compared with RMB0.08 for the same period of 2025.

Other Information

As of September 30, 2026, Youdao's cash, cash equivalents, current and non-current restricted cash, time deposits and short-term investments totaled RMB599.8 million (US$89.5 million), compared with RMB743.2 million as of December 31, 2025. For the third quarter of 2026, net cash used in operating activities was RMB89.0 million (US$13.3 million). Youdao's ability to continue as a going concern is dependent on management's ability to implement an effective business plan amid a changing regulatory environment, generate operating cash flows, and secure external financing for future development. As of September 30, 2026, Youdao has received various forms of financial support from NetEase Group, including, among others, RMB748.0 million in a short-term loan, and US$120.4 million in long-term loans maturing on March 31, 2030, drawn from a US$300.0 million revolving loan facility.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company's contract liabilities, which mainly consisted of deferred revenues generated from Youdao's learning services, were RMB771.8 million (US$115.1 million), compared with RMB847.7 million as of December 31, 2025.

Share Repurchase Program

On November 17, 2022, the Company announced that its Board of Directors had authorized the Company to adopt a share repurchase program in accordance with applicable laws and regulations for up to US$20.0 million of its Class A ordinary shares (including in the form of ADSs) during a period of up to 36 months beginning on November 18, 2022. This amount was subsequently increased to US$40.0 million in August 2023. In November 2025 and August 2026, the Board approved amendments to this Program, each extending its expiration date by one year, ultimately to November 17, 2027. As of September 30, 2026, the Company had repurchased a total of approximately 7.5 million ADSs in the open market under the share repurchase program for a total consideration of approximately US$33.8 million.

SHENZHEN, China, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- MoonFox Data, the full-scenario data insight and analytics specialist under Aurora Mobile (NASDAQ: JG), today set out how its China large language model (LLM) usage dataset gives global investors and research firms a continuous view of how much each leading Chinese model is actually being used — a measure that no provider publishes on a standardized, ongoing basis.

Competition among China's large language models is now decided on usage. Which model is gaining volume, which is losing share, and how quickly a price cut or a new release reorders the field are questions that investors ask every week. The answers sit in model usage data, and that data is largely invisible from outside: Chinese model providers do not disclose usage or share continuously, and an overseas firm cannot observe it without local data sources, long-term engineering and a compliance framework built for the purpose.

What the dataset provides

MoonFox Data model usage data is built to be consumed, not merely referenced. Delivered by API, it provides:

  • Model-level usage volume across China's leading large language models, tracked on a continuous basis rather than reconstructed from filings or one-off studies.
  • Share and trend views that make relative movement between models measurable over time, including the effect of price changes, new model releases and feature updates.
  • High-frequency updates with point-in-time (PIT) history, so a series can be read as it stood on a given date rather than as it looks after later revisions.
  • A clear licensing and compliance chain, covering data sourcing, processing and redistribution, which institutional users require before a dataset can enter research and client-facing products.

How institutions use it

MoonFox Data model usage data supports three recurring workflows:

  1. Tracking the model landscape. Analysts monitor relative usage across models to identify structural shifts in share, rather than relying on announcements or anecdotal signals.
  2. Measuring event impact. Around a new model launch, a price cut or a promotion, the data shows how large the change in usage is and whether it is a short-lived spike or a lift in the underlying level.
  3. Building research products. Data teams ingest the series into their own pipelines, apply their modeling and quality control, and deliver structured China AI signals to their investment clients.

In use at a global research firm

The dataset is already in production use. A global alternative data research firm takes the series by API and runs it through two workflows: its analysts use it to track relative usage across models and to size the effect of launches and price changes, while its data team ingests the same series into its own pipeline, applies its modeling and quality control, and delivers the resulting China AI signals to institutional investors. The data enters the firm's client-facing research products as an underlying source rather than a one-off reference, a path that demands stable definitions, continuous delivery and an auditable licensing chain.

Part of a broader China data portfolio

MoonFox Data model usage data sits alongside the company's wider alternative data offering, which draws on more than 200 million daily active devices and a history dating to 2019. The portfolio covers mobile app activity, AI application and mini-program engagement, brand and marketing insight, and financial alternative data, and is available through API, data feed or custom delivery.

About MoonFox Data

As a sub-brand of Aurora Mobile (NASDAQ: JG), MoonFox Data is a leading expert in data insights and alternative data services, trusted by top-tier global investment banks, hedge funds, and leading PE/VC firms. Powered by a comprehensive, secure, and fully compliant omnichannel big data foundation, we leverage advanced AI algorithms and predictive modeling to deliver unparalleled data capabilities. Through our core offerings—including MoonFox Alternative Data, iAPP, iBrand, iMarketing, and the professional consulting services of MoonFox Research—we transform massive datasets into actionable intelligence. MoonFox Data is dedicated to empowering institutional investors and enterprise clients to uncover hidden market trends, generate alpha, and make highly accurate, data-driven decisions.

— SYVIK® becomes the first novel Syk inhibitor approved in China — 

— Simultaneous approvals in two underserved autoimmune indications supported by positive ESLIM-01 trial in ITP and ESLIM-02 trial in wAIHA —

— Expands HUTCHMED’s commercial portfolio into immunology, establishing a new presence beyond oncology — 

HONG KONG, SHANGHAI and FLORHAM PARK, N.J., Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- HUTCHMED (China) Limited (“HUTCHMED”) (Nasdaq/AIM:​HCM; HKEX:​13) today announces that the China National Medical Products Administration (“NMPA”) has granted simultaneous approval for two New Drug Applications (NDAs) of SYVIK® (sovleplenib), a novel, selective oral small molecule inhibitor targeting spleen tyrosine kinase (“Syk”):

  • Immune Thrombocytopenia (“ITP”): For the treatment of adult patients with chronic primary ITP who have had an insufficient response to at least one prior therapy; and
  • Warm Antibody Autoimmune Hemolytic Anemia (“wAIHA”): For the treatment of adult patients with wAIHA who who have had an insufficient response to prior corticosteroid therapy.

The approval for ITP is supported by data from ESLIM-01 (NCT05029635), a randomized, double-blinded, placebo-controlled Phase III trial in China of SYVIK® in 188 adult patients who had received at least one prior line of standard therapy. Results from ESLIM-01 study were published in The Lancet Haematology. SYVIK® demonstrated a clinically meaningful early and sustained durable platelet response in patients with primary ITP compared to placebo, with durable response rate of 48.4% compared to zero with placebo (p<0.0001). Overall response rates were 68.3% at 0–12 weeks and 70.6% at 0–24 weeks with SYVIK®, compared to 14.5% and 16.1% with placebo (p<0.0001). SYVIK® demonstrated a tolerable safety profile and improvement in quality of life. 

The approval for wAIHA is supported by data from ESLIM-02 (NCT05535933), a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase II/III study in adult patients with primary or secondary wAIHA who had relapsed or were refractory to prior glucocorticoid treatment. Results from the Phase II part of ESLIM-02 were published in The Lancet Haematology. Results from the Phase III part were presented at the European Hematology Association (“EHA”) 2026 Congress. SYVIK® demonstrated a significantly higher durable response rate during weeks 5–24 compared to placebo (66% vs 15%, p<0.0001). During the 24-week double-blind treatment period, SYVIK® demonstrated superior efficacy across several key metrics; specifically, the overall response rate — defined as hemoglobin ≥100 g/L with an increase of ≥20 g/L from baseline without rescue therapy — was significantly increased (70% vs 22%, p<0.0001). SYVIK® demonstrated a favorable safety profile with no treatment-related deaths or discontinuations in the SYVIK® group.

Mr Johnny Cheng, Acting Chief Executive Officer and Chief Financial Officer of HUTCHMED, said: “The simultaneous approvals of SYVIK® for both ITP and wAIHA represent a significant milestone for HUTCHMED as our first in-house discovered immunology drug approved for commercialization. Patients with these chronic autoimmune blood conditions often face disease relapses and tolerability challenges associated with prolonged standard treatments. SYVIK® has demonstrated clinically meaningful efficacy, rapid onset, and sustained durable responses with a favorable safety profile across the pivotal ESLIM-01 and ESLIM-02 studies. We are committed to making this new targeted treatment option accessible to patients across China, addressing critical unmet needs and helping patients better manage these challenging conditions.”

In addition to the regulatory approvals in China, sovleplenib was granted Orphan Drug Designation by the US FDA for the treatment of primary ITP and autoimmune hemolytic anemia in October 2026. This designation underscores the clinical value of sovleplenib and its potential to address significant unmet medical needs on a global scale. HUTCHMED retains full worldwide rights to sovleplenib and continues to evaluate strategic pathways to support its global development.

About ITP

ITP is an autoimmune disorder characterized by immunologic destruction of platelets and decreased platelet production. Patients with ITP are at increased risk of excessive bleeding and bruising.1 ITP is also associated with fatigue (reported in up to 39% of adults with ITP) and impaired quality of life.2,3,4,5,6 The incidence of primary ITP in adults is 3.3/100,000 adults per year with a prevalence of 9.5 per 100,000 adults.7 Based on this prevalence rate, approximately 110,000 patients are estimated to be living with primary ITP in China, in addition to 56,000 patients in the US, Germany, France, Italy, Spain, UK, and Japan. It has been estimated that as many as 145,000 patients are living with chronic ITP in major pharmaceutical markets excluding China.8

Adult ITP is a heterogeneous disease that can persist for years, even with best available care, and treatments are infrequently curative. Despite availability of several treatments with differing mechanisms of action, chronicity of disease continues to be a problem. Many patients develop resistance to treatment and thereby are prone to relapse.9 Thus, there remains a significant population of patients who have limited sensitivity to currently available agents and are in need of new treatments.

As platelet destruction in ITP is mediated by Syk-dependent phagocytosis of FcγR-bound platelets, Syk inhibition represents a promising approach to management of ITP.10

About wAIHA

Autoimmune hemolytic anemia (“AIHA”) is an autoimmune disorder characterized by the destruction of red blood cells (“RBCs”) due to the production of antibodies against RBC. The incidence of AIHA is estimated to be 0.8-3.0/100,000 adults per year with an estimated prevalence of 17 per 100,000 adults and a death rate of 8-11%.11,12 wAIHA is the most common form of AIHA,13 accounting for about 75-80% of all adult AIHA cases.14

The accelerated clearance of antibody-coated RBCs by immunoglobulin Fc-gamma receptor (FcγR) bearing macrophages is thought to be the pathogenic mechanism in wAIHA.15 Activated Syk mediates downstream signaling of the activated Fc receptors in phagocytic cells, resulting in phagocytosis of RBCs.16 In addition, activation of Syk through the B-cell receptor mediates activation and differentiation of B-lymphocytes into antibody secreting plasma cells.17 Inhibition of Syk may have potential effects in the treatment of wAIHA through inhibition of phagocytosis and reduction of antibody production.

About SYVIK®

SYVIK® (sovleplenib) is a novel, selective inhibitor of Syk. Syk is a major component in B-cell receptor and FcR signaling and is an established target for the treatment of multiple subtypes of B-cell lymphomas and autoimmune disorders.

HUTCHMED currently retains all rights to sovleplenib worldwide. 

About HUTCHMED

HUTCHMED (Nasdaq/AIM:HCM; HKEX:13) is an innovative, commercial-stage, biopharmaceutical company. It is committed to the discovery and global development and commercialization of targeted therapies and immunotherapies for the treatment of cancer and immunological diseases. Since inception it has focused on bringing drug candidates from in-house discovery to patients around the world, with its first five medicines marketed in China, the first of which is also approved around the world including in the US, Europe and Japan.
