VANCOUVER, BC, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Vizsla Silver Corp. (TSX: VZLA) (NYSE: VZLA) (Frankfurt: 0G3) ("Vizsla Silver" or the "Company") is providing an update on the continued advancement of its wholly owned Panuco silver-gold project ("Panuco" or the "Project") in Mexico. 

Vizsla Silver continues to advance key development activities at Panuco with a focus on construction readiness. M3 Engineering & Technology has now completed approximately 50% of engineering and approximately 85% of the process plant equipment currently contemplated for the Project has been ordered. As previously disclosed, three key development contracts for the Project have been awarded, including engineering procurement and construction management (EPCM), mine design and equipment supply (see press releases dated April 23, 2026 and June 16, 2026, respectively), with the main mining contract to be awarded in due course. In parallel, the Company continues to work closely with Mexican federal authorities to strengthen security arrangements in preparation for a phased return to site.

"We have made significant progress advancing Panuco this year, achieving important milestones in engineering, procurement and development planning," said Michael Konnert, President and Chief Executive Officer. "We are well positioned to  move into the next phase of development, with safety guiding our preparations for a phased return to site and first silver production now anticipated in the second half of 2028."

"This progress has come during an exceptionally difficult year, and we have remained focused on supporting our people, their families and the communities in which we operate. We stand by the families of our colleagues and share their grief in this profound loss, as well as their need for answers. We continue to support the Mexican authorities in their ongoing investigation. Our commitment to the families of our colleagues is enduring, as is our belief in Panuco's future and its potential to create lasting opportunities for the communities in Sinaloa and the people of Mexico."

Long-term Support and the Vizsla Foundation 

Since February 2026, Vizsla Silver has been working toward establishing the Vizsla Foundation (the "Foundation") as part of its long-term commitment to the people and communities of Sinaloa. The Foundation is intended to complement the direct assistance the Company continues to provide to the families impacted by the tragic events of January 2026 by focusing on providing meaningful, publicly available, multigenerational support and lasting opportunities to individuals and families across local communities.

The Company continues to engage with the local communities to help shape the Foundation's priorities and long-term initiatives, including support for education, health and economic development in the communities surrounding Panuco. Further details regarding the Foundation's structure and programs will be shared as plans progress and discussions with families continue.

Vizsla Silver has committed to making an initial contribution of US$5 million to the Foundation, with plans to also direct a percentage of future profits toward sustaining its work.

Security and Site Readiness 

The safety of employees and contractors remains central and continues to guide the Company's planning for a return to site. Vizsla Silver continues to work closely with Mexican federal authorities and third-party security advisors to support additional security infrastructure, enhance overall security measures and strengthen on-site support in preparation for a phased return. These efforts build on the Company's established approach to security, which has included a significant investment in security resources, third-party risk assessments and adjustments to or suspension of activities in response to changing conditions. The timing and scope of any formal return to the project site will be informed by the Company's assessment of security conditions and readiness.

Updated Project Guidance 

The Company has revised its targeted first silver production at Panuco to H2 2028, from H2 2027, previously. The revised development schedule reflects the Company's current expectations for permitting, site readiness and construction timing.

Except for the updated development timeline, the Company is not updating the operating, capital or economic parameters disclosed in the Company's November 2025 Feasibility Study (the "Feasibility Study"). GUIYANG, China, Nov. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Full Truck Alliance Co. Ltd. ("FTA" or the "Company") (NYSE: YMM), a leading digital freight platform, today announced its unaudited financial results for the third quarter ended September 30, 2026.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial and Operational Highlights

  • Total net revenues in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB3,585.7 million (US$534.8 million), an increase of 6.8% from RMB3,358.2 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Net income in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,372.5 million (US$204.7 million), an increase of 49.0% from RMB921.0 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Non-GAAP adjusted net income1 in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,452.8 million (US$216.7 million), an increase of 47.0% from RMB988.1 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Fulfilled orders2 in the third quarter of 2026 reached 70.6 million, an increase of 11.3% from 63.4 million in the same period of 2025.

  • Average shipper MAUs3 in the third quarter of 2026 reached 3.76 million, an increase of 12.4% from 3.35 million in the same period of 2025.

Mr. Peter Hui Zhang, Founder, Chairman, and Chief Executive Officer of FTA, commented, "In the third quarter, we continued to grow our user base on both sides of the platform, with particularly strong growth in direct shippers. Efficient cargo finding, together with stronger transaction protection, helped us improve truckers' retention and fulfillment frequency. We also leveraged deeper route-level supply-demand data analysis to upgrade our algorithms, which further improved the overall fulfillment rate. Going forward, we will continue to improve the customer experience through diversified service offerings such as entrusted service for direct shippers, express cargo delivery and top-rated trucker program. We will further integrate AI agents into capacity dispatching across a wider range of routes, further improving fulfillment efficiency. In terms of overseas development, Qmove now operates in five markets, and we will continue to grow its user base and order volume."

Mr. Langbo Guo, President of FTA, added, "Total net revenues reached RMB3.59 billion this quarter, up 6.8% year over year. Transaction service revenues grew steadily, rising 25.0% year over year to RMB1.82 billion. Operating efficiency continued to improve, with net income up 49.0% year over year to RMB1.37 billion and non-GAAP adjusted net income up 47.0% to RMB1.45 billion. Thanks to sustained profit growth and the steady transition of our credit solutions business, net cash provided by operating activities was RMB3.16 billion this quarter, providing us with ample liquidity to support new business initiatives."

1 Non-GAAP adjusted net income is defined as net income excluding (i) share-based compensation expense; (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from business acquisitions; (iii) losses (gains) on equity investments measured at fair value; and (iv) tax effects of non-GAAP adjustments. See "Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures" and "Reconciliations of GAAP and Non-GAAP Results" at the end of this press release.

2 Fulfilled orders on our platform in a given period are defined as all shipping orders matched through our platform during such period but exclude (i) shipping orders that are subsequently canceled and (ii) shipping orders for which our users failed to specify any freight prices, as there are substantial uncertainties as to whether such shipping orders are fulfilled.

3 Average shipper MAUs in a given period are calculated by dividing (i) the sum of shipper MAUs for each month of a given period by (ii) the number of months in a given period. Shipper MAUs are defined as the number of active shippers on our platform in a given month. Active shippers are defined as the aggregate number of registered shipper accounts that have posted at least one shipping order on our platform during a given period.

Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results

Net Revenues (including value added taxes, or "VAT" of RMB1,222.9 million and RMB719.6 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025 and 2026, respectively). Total net revenues in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB3,585.7 million (US$534.8 million), representing an increase of 6.8% from RMB3,358.2 million in the same period of 2025, primarily attributable to an increase in revenues from freight matching services.

Freight matching services. Revenues from freight matching services in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB3,254.4 million (US$485.4 million), representing an increase of 16.3% from RMB2,797.6 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was mainly due to the sustained increase in transaction service revenues.

  • Freight brokerage service. Revenues from freight brokerage service in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB1,194.8 million (US$178.2 million), representing an increase of 9.2% from RMB1,094.3 million in the same period of 2025, primarily attributable to an increase in service fee rate, partially offset by a decrease in transaction volume.

  • Freight listing service. Revenues from freight listing service in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB240.0 million (US$35.8 million), compared with RMB247.1 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to a decrease in the number of total paying members.

  • Transaction service. Revenues from transaction service amounted to RMB1,819.6 million (US$271.4 million) in the third quarter of 2026, an increase of 25.0% from RMB1,456.1 million in the same period of 2025, primarily driven by increases in order volume, penetration rate and per-order transaction service fee.

Value-added services.4 Revenues from value-added services in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB331.3 million (US$49.4 million), compared with RMB560.7 million in the same period of 2025. The decrease was primarily due to a decrease in credit solutions revenues.

Cost of Revenues (including VAT net of government grants of RMB1,033.9 million and RMB652.0 million for the three months ended September 30, 2025 and 2026, respectively). Cost of revenues in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,026.1 million (US$153.1 million), compared with RMB1,605.2 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to decreases in VAT, related tax surcharges and other tax costs, net of grants from government authorities. These tax-related costs net of government grants totaled RMB816.8 million, compared with RMB1,427.2 million in the same period of 2025, primarily due to a decrease in tax costs net of government grants related to the Company's freight brokerage service.

Sales and Marketing Expenses. Sales and marketing expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB446.0 million (US$66.5 million), compared with RMB438.8 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily due to additional investments to support the expansion of the Company's overseas business, partially offset by efficiency-focused spending on domestic user acquisition.

General and Administrative Expenses. General and administrative expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB166.8 million (US$24.9 million), compared with RMB161.6 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was primarily due to higher share-based compensation expenses.

Research and Development Expenses. Research and development expenses in the third quarter of 2026 were RMB289.8 million (US$43.2 million), compared with RMB233.3 million in the same period of 2025. The increase was mainly due to ongoing R&D investment in new business initiatives.

Income from Operations. Income from operations in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,609.8 million (US$240.1 million), an increase of 107.4% from RMB776.3 million in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP Adjusted Operating Income.5 Non-GAAP adjusted operating income in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,683.5 million (US$251.1 million), an increase of 98.3% from RMB849.1 million in the same period of 2025.

Net Income. Net income in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,372.5 million (US$204.7 million), an increase of 49.0% from RMB921.0 million in the same period of 2025.

Non-GAAP Adjusted Net Income. Non-GAAP adjusted net income in the third quarter of 2026 was RMB1,452.8 million (US$216.7 million), an increase of 47.0% from RMB988.1 million in the same period of 2025.

Basic and Diluted Net Income per ADS6 and Non-GAAP Adjusted Basic and Diluted Net Income per ADS.7 Basic net income per ADS was RMB1.31 (US$0.20) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.87 in the same period of 2025. Diluted net income per ADS was RMB1.30 (US$0.19) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.87 in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP adjusted basic net income per ADS was RMB1.38 (US$0.21) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.94 in the same period of 2025. Non-GAAP adjusted diluted net income per ADS was RMB1.38 (US$0.21) in the third quarter of 2026, compared with RMB0.93 in the same period of 2025.

Balance Sheet and Cash Flow

As of September 30, 2026, the Company had cash and cash equivalents, restricted cash, time deposits and wealth management products of RMB35.5 billion (US$5.3 billion) in total, compared with RMB31.5 billion as of December 31, 2025.

As of September 30, 2026, the total outstanding loan balance8 was RMB2.5 billion (US$0.4 billion), a decrease of 54.4% from RMB5.5 billion as of December 31, 2025. The total non-performing loan ratio8 was 4.7% as of September 30, 2026, compared with 2.9% as of December 31, 2025, primarily due to the migration of previously delinquent balances to outstanding loans that were over 90 calendar days past due, compounded by a rapidly reduced total outstanding loan balance.

In the third quarter of 2026, net cash provided by operating activities was RMB3,164.2 million (US$471.9 million), compared with RMB1,657.1 million in the same period of 2025. Free cash flow9 was RMB3,040.0 million (US$453.4 million), compared with RMB1,608.5 million in the same period of 2025.

Business Outlook

The Company expects its total net revenues to be between RMB3.19 billion and RMB3.29 billion for the fourth quarter of 2026, representing approximately flat to a 3.1% year-over-year increase. These forecasts are based on the Company's current and preliminary view of the market and operational conditions, which are subject to change and cannot be predicted with reasonable accuracy as of the date hereof.

Declaration of Quarterly Cash Dividend

Pursuant to the Company's shareholder return plan, the board approved a cash dividend for the fourth quarter of 2026 in the amount of US$0.0042 per ordinary share, or US$0.0840 per ADS, totaling approximately US$87.5 million. About Full Truck Alliance Co. Ltd.

Full Truck Alliance Co. Ltd. (NYSE: YMM) is a leading digital freight platform connecting shippers with truckers to facilitate shipments across distance ranges, cargo weights and types. The Company provides a range of freight matching services, including freight listing, freight brokerage and transaction services. The Company also provides a range of value-added services that cater to the various needs of shippers and truckers, while enabling other businesses, such as financial institutions, highway authorities and gas station operators, to participate in its ecosystem. With a mission to empower enterprises with greater logistics competitiveness, the Company is shaping the future of logistics with technology and aspires to revolutionize logistics, improve efficiency across the value chain and reduce its carbon footprint for our planet. Use of Non-GAAP Financial Measures

The Company uses non-GAAP adjusted operating income, non-GAAP adjusted net income, non-GAAP adjusted net income attributable to ordinary shareholders, non-GAAP adjusted basic and diluted net income per share, non-GAAP adjusted basic and diluted net income per ADS and free cash flow, each a non-GAAP financial measure, as supplemental measures to review and assess its operating performance.

The presentation of non-GAAP financial measures is not intended to be considered in isolation or as a substitute for the financial information prepared and presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The Company defines non-GAAP adjusted operating income as income from operations excluding (i) share-based compensation expense; and (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from business acquisitions. The Company defines non-GAAP adjusted net income as net income excluding (i) share-based compensation expense; (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from business acquisitions; (iii) losses (gains) on equity investments measured at fair value; and (iv) tax effects of non-GAAP adjustments. The Company defines non-GAAP adjusted net income attributable to ordinary shareholders as net income attributable to ordinary shareholders excluding (i) share-based compensation expense; (ii) amortization of intangible assets resulting from business acquisitions; (iii) losses (gains) on equity investments measured at fair value; and (iv) tax effects of non-GAAP adjustments. The Company defines non-GAAP adjusted basic and diluted net income per share as non-GAAP adjusted net income attributable to ordinary shareholders divided by weighted average number of basic and diluted ordinary shares, respectively. The Company defines non-GAAP adjusted basic and diluted net income per ADS as non-GAAP adjusted net income attributable to ordinary shareholders divided by the weighted average number of basic and diluted ADSs, respectively. The Company defines free cash flow as operating cash flow adjusted for the impact from capital expenditures. Capital expenditures include purchase of property and equipment and intangible assets.

The non-GAAP financial measures are not defined under U.S. GAAP and are not presented in accordance with U.S. GAAP. The non-GAAP financial measures have limitations as an analytical tool. The non-GAAP financial measures do not reflect all items of expense that affect its operations.

The Company reconciles the non-GAAP financial measures to the nearest U.S. GAAP performance measures. VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 19, 2026 / American Critical Minerals Corp. ("American Critical Minerals" or the "Company") (CSE:KCLI)(OTCQB:APCOF)(Frankfurt:2P3) is pleased to announce that it has received assay results from the Duma Point AP-S-02 well, at the Company's Green River Project located 20 miles northwest of Moab, Utah. The highest-grade assay results returned a composite grade of 42.94 weight per cent ("wt.%") KCl over 2.1 metres ("m") (7 feet) within the Cycle 5 potash member. Geochemical assay data confirm robust potash bed thicknesses and grades, underscoring the high-grade characteristic of the potash mineralization within this area of the Green River Project and the Paradox Basin.

HIGHLIGHTS

  • Assay results and downhole wireline geophysical logs returned a composite grade of 38.51 wt.% KCl over 6.55m or 21.5 feet within the Cycle 5 potash member. High-grade potash with meaningful thickness has now been confirmed at the Green River Project.
  • Results represent an 11% increase in thickness and a 51% increase in grade compared with the historic Quintana Fed 1-1 well located 600m (~ 2,000 feet) east-northeast of the current well 1 .
  • Includes a high composite grade intersection of 42.94 wt.% over 2.1m (6.9 feet).
  • The presence and continuity of sylvite mineralization within the Cycle 5 potash bed now de-risks the historical potash data reported on and available from within the Green River Project.
  • Potash results compare favorably to reported grades from the nearby Moab Solution Mine which produces potash from the same Cycle 5 potash bed 5 .
  • Potash results from the inaugural well on the Green River Project have delivered one of the highest-grade potash intersections globally.

Dean Pekeski, President and CEO stated, "Having completed our inaugural drill program at the Green River Project and we are extremely happy with the results. The potash results are exceptional and highlight the strong pedigree we believed exists within this Property. The significant improvement in both potash grade and thickness versus what was drilled historically validates our targeting exercise and bodes well for future resource delineation. This is a defining moment for our Company and represents the first step in moving this Project forward. Planning for an additional 1-2 wells will commence now with the goal being to generate an NI 43-101 compliant resource and Scoping Study. The Green River Project is progressing while the United States recognizes that critical need for secure fertilizer supply chains."

The Duma Point AP-S-02 Well

The purpose of the Duma Point AP-S-02 well (the "well") was to validate historic drill data and test, through coring and brine sampling, the key Paradox formation potash horizons as well as the clastic brine-bearing zones for lithium and bromine in the Paradox and Leadville formations. Figure 1 shows the location of the Duma Point AP-S-02 well.

Figure 1. - Location map showing the Duma Point AP-S-02 well

Coring operations targeting the Cycle 5 potash member commenced at a depth of 1,741m (5,712 feet) below surface. The core run was planned to recover 45.72m (150 feet) of 4-inch drill core. Due to tight hole conditions causing core loss, core recovery was limited to 25.25m (82.85 feet) with the bottom 20.47 metres (67.15 feet) being lost in the hole. The cored interval did successfully recover 5.54m (18.17 feet) of sylvite mineralization from the Cycle 5 potash member.

To complement the core recovery and aquifer identification, the Company acquired a comprehensive suite of downhole wireline geophysical logs ( "e-logs") to characterize the subsurface stratigraphy and support interpretation of the targeted potash and brine bearing intervals 6 .

The Duma Point AP-S-02 reached a total depth of 2,818 metres (9,245 feet). The well has been cemented and abandoned according to requirements and stipulations found within the State permit for the well, and the drill rig was demobilized on September 25, 2026.

Potash Results

In total, 5.54m (18.17 feet) of sylvite mineralized drill core from the Cycle 5 potash member was recovered (see Figure 2 and Table 1). The downhole wireline geophysical logs show that 1.01m (3.33 feet) of potash mineralized core was lost, meaning that the Cycle 5 potash intersection cut by the well was 6.55m (21.5 feet). In the absence of assays from the lost section of Cycle 5 potash core, downhole wireline geophysical logs results were used to determine the potash content for that interval. 6 There was a strong correlation between the assay results and the downhole wireline geophysical logs for the cored interval.

The vertical well was drilled at Lat: 38.749405, Long: -110.0044758. Based on downhole directional drilling tests and the vertical nature of the stratigraphy interpreted from seismic data the samples are believed to represent true thickness. The 5,794.85-to-5,798.18-foot interval was dropped/lost. Results for this interval are reported from e-logs.

The drill core and completed wireline data confirmed the presence of the Cycle 5 potash unit consistent with historic drilling results from the Quintana Fed 1-1 well, located approximately 0.6 kilometres (~ 2,000 feet) east-northeast of the current well. The Quintana Fed 1-1 well intersected the Cycle 5 potash bed reporting a grade of 24.3% eKCl from elogs over a thickness of 5.9m (19.4 feet).

Recovered core was logged, photographed, sampled, and transported from Rapid City to the Saskatchewan Research Council laboratories in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, for geochemical analysis. Twenty-one halved core samples were collected and shipped under the supervision of qualified independent geological personnel for analysis using industry-standard procedures. Quality assurance and quality control protocols included the insertion of blanks, standards, and duplicate samples throughout the sampling program. Assays were completed along the entire length of recovered core. Core was also retained for future geo-mechanical testing.

Assays from the recovered drill core returned a composite grade of 35.4 wt.% KCl over 5.54m (18.17 feet) in the Cycle 5 potash member assuming a 5% K 2 O cut-off. Composite carnallite and insoluble content was very low with each reporting <0.1 wt.% and <1.0 wt.% respectively. Included in this assayed interval was a high-grade interval which comprised 2.1m (7 feet) of potash core with a composite grade of 42.94 wt.% KCl (5,780 to 5,787 feet). Table 1 summarizes the assay results from this drill hole.

Figure 2. - Duma Point AP-S-02 photograph of high-grade zone drill core

Adjusting for the lost drill core, the Duma Point AP-S-02 assays and downhole wireline geophysical logs returned a composite grade of 38.51 wt.% KCl over 6.55m (21.5 feet) within the Cycle 5 potash member.

Geochemical assay data and grade interpretations from the e-logs confirm robust potash bed thicknesses and grades, underscoring the high-grade character of mineralization within this area of the Green River Project and Paradox Basin. Figure 3 shows how the grade from the Duma Point AP-S-02 well compares with average KCl grades from other potash projects in North America. The intersection reported represents an 11% increase in thickness and a 51% increase in grade compared with the historical e-logs from the Quintana Fed 1-1 well.

The Company has no affiliation to any of these Companies or Projects.

Lithium and Bromine Aquifers

Two short-duration drill stem packer tests were completed targeting the Leadville Formation limestone unit (2,670 to 2,815 m or 8,760.2 to 9,236 feet), and lower clastic units of the Paradox Formation (2,144 to 2,181m or 7,035 to 7,155 feet). Although brine was successfully sampled from the Leadville Formation test, meaningful lithium and bromine results were not obtained. Future longer duration pumping tests could provide different results. The sample collected from the Paradox Formation was contaminated with drilling fluids/mud and deemed to be inconclusive. Given these results and the high-cost nature of drilling to these depths, the Company will re-evaluate future drilling and sampling programs within these deep zones.

About American Critical Minerals' Green River Potash and Lithium Project

The Green River Project is situated within Utah's highly productive Paradox Basin, located 20 miles northwest of Moab, Utah. It has significant logistical advantages including close proximity to major rail hubs, airport, roads, water, towns, and labour markets. It also benefits from close proximity to the agricultural and industrial heartland of America and numerous potential end-users for its products.

The history of oil and gas production across the Paradox Basin provides geologic data from historic wells across the Project, and the wider Basin, validating and de-risking the potential for high grade potash and large amounts of contained lithium. Wells in and around the project reported lithium up to 500 ppm, bromine up to 6,100 ppm and boron up to 1,260 ppm (Gilbride & Santos, 2012). This data is reinforced by nearby potash production and the advanced stage of neighbouring lithium projects. The Paradox Basin is believed to be one of the biggest sources of lithium brines in the United States. (Source: AnsonFastmarketsPresentation- https://wcsecure.weblink.com.au/pdf/ASN/02823465.pdf ) .1

The Company has disclosed targets for further exploration at the Green River Project consisting of 500 million to 950 million tonnes of sylvinite (the most important source for the production of potash in North America) 4 grading from 12% to 18% potassium oxide based on elog (eK2O=19% to 29% potassium chloride based on elog (eKCl)). Its target for further exploration for Lithium and Bromine is 2.1 billion cubic meters brine volume grading 71.6 to 216.3 ppm Li and 3,656 to 4,741 ppm Br. 2

The Company holds a 100% interest in eleven SITLA mineral and minerals salt leases covering approximately 7,050 acres, 1,094 federal lithium brine claims (BLM Placer Claims) covering 21,150 acres, and 11 federal (BLM) potash prospecting permits covering approximately 25,480 acres. Through these leases, permits and claims the Company has the ability to explore for potash, lithium, and potential by-products across the entire Green River Project (approx. 32,530 acres). The Company is authorized to drill a total of 7 drill holes across the Green River Project.

America's largest potash company and only U.S. domestic potash producer currently produces potash from its nearby Moab Solution Mine, which the Company believes provides strong evidence of stratigraphic continuity within this part of the Paradox Basin 5 . Anson Resources Ltd. has advanced lithium development projects contiguous to the northern boundary of our Green River Project and neighbouring to the south. 5 Anson has a large initial resource, robust definitive feasibility study and has recently completed successful piloting operations through its partnership with Koch Technology Solutions, as well as an offtake agreement with LG Energy Solution. The Anson exploration targets encompass the combined Mississippian Leadville Formation and the Pennsylvanian Paradox Formation brine-bearing clastic layers, which also underlie American Critical Minerals' entire project area (www.ansonresources.com). 3

The United States imports more than 90% of its potash demand (U.S. Geological Survey, Mineral Commodity Summaries, January 2025). In November 2025, the Department of Interior added potash to its list of Critical Minerals which already includes lithium. Recent market estimates suggest that the global potash market is over US$50 billion annually and growing at a compound annual growth rate ("CAGR") of close to 5%. Annual lithium demand is now estimated to be over 1 million tonnes globally and continuing to grow rapidly. 4
